title: An exploration request that never names a skill loads the project-explorer workflow, and the answer comes from the code
prompt: 我刚接手这个项目，先别改任何东西。讲清它是干什么的：入口在哪个文件、启动后默认监听哪个端口、对外有哪些 HTTP 路由。

fixture.notes: A four-module service. README deliberately omits the port and the route list; both exist only in code, so an answer that names them was read rather than guessed.

graders.expects: every read_skill call used name=project-explorer; no other workflow was loaded instead
the answer names main.py as the entry point
the answer names the default port 8765, which appears only in service/main.py
graders.evidence: final assistant text against the fixture's DEFAULT_PORT

graders.expects: the answer names the /health route, which appears only in service/routes.py
graders.evidence: final assistant text against the fixture's ROUTES

cleanup: Discard the trial workspace; the fixture directory is never written to.
notes: The prompt asks for what any owner would ask and never names a skill: whether project-explorer is loaded is the model's own decision, which is the thing measured. The three answer graders exist to stop a pass that reads the skill and then describes a project it never opened; they do not grade the quality of the description, and a run that reads the skill but names no port still fails here. Whether the answer follows the skill's own outline stays semantic and unasserted.
